newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-CHILAVERT BURIES THE HATCHET WITH OLD FOES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CHILAVERT BURIES THE HATCHET WITH OLD FOES.

text.p: Paraguayan international goalkeeper Jose Luis Chilavert, in an unusually mellow mood, said on Wednesday he was prepared to bury the hatchet with his old foes Diego Maradona and former Argentina captain Oscar Ruggeri.
"Maradona and I are both big personalities and intelligent personalities," said Chilavert, who also broke his silence on the player strike which paralysed the Argentine championship at the weekend.
"We could go and have coffee and sort out our differences. I would be prepared to have a chat with him because face to face we could sort everything out.
"Diego is extremely motivated at the moment and that is contagious," he added, referring to Maradona's umpteenth comeback earlier this month.

Chilavert, who almost makes a hobby out of engaging other players in verbal warfare, also found some rare compliments for Ruggeri, the rugged defender who is his country's most-capped player and now at the forefront of the strike.
"Ruggeri is defending the players which is something I support," he said of a player with whom he has almost come to blows on more than one occasion.

Last year Chilavert, who plays for the Buenos Aires club Velez Sarsfield, hinted that Ruggeri had deliberately tried to injure him during an championship match played shortly before Argentina met Paraguay in a World Cup qualifier.
But on Wednesday he said: "Ruggeri and I have always sorted out our differences in our own way on the pitch, just as you do in a Sunday league match. But at the moment I am on his side."
Ruggeri, who retired from international soccer after the 1994 World Cup but continues playing for Buenos Aires club San Lorenzo, has been one of the forces behind the strike.
Chilavert, who has broken the goalkeeping mould by becoming a free kick and penalty specialist, has been unusually subdued since the affair began but said on Wednesday he backed the strikers.

The stoppage began last week in support of six players with first division club Deportivo Espanol. A judge ruled the players count as assets of the heavily indebted club and cannot leave until all creditors have been paid.
